subject.title: [TUI] Scroll-jump / auto-scroll behavior is still disruptive in 2026.3.8

question: Should the TUI fix disruptive scroll jumps primarily by repairing renderer/viewport anchoring, by adding an explicit TUI auto-scroll or preserve mode, or by waiting for live reproduction/upstream pi-tui resolution before implementation?
rationale: The source path is credible, but the permanent fix changes terminal UX behavior and may require either third-party renderer ownership or a new user-facing TUI mode.

options.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
options.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

options.title: Add explicit TUI scroll mode
options.body: Expose a terminal user control for follow behavior, accepting the extra option/docs/tests and fresh-install or upgrade proof burden.

options.title: Wait for upstream or live proof
options.body: Keep the tracker open until a current-main terminal capture or upstream pi-tui patch proves the exact repair path.

recommendation.title: Repair renderer and anchoring
recommendation.body: Prefer a live-proven fix that prevents content-driven redraws from clearing or jumping scrollback, then follows new output only when the user is already at the tail.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent history in the TUI ChatLog/event-handler state path that would need the decision translated into an implementation.
